digest.component_or_area: snapshot cache janitor and repo-snapshot store
propositions: _gc_pass reads only free disk space and mtime, never consulting the incrementally-maintained byte_total counter promised by ADR 0005 and the janitor's own contract docstring, leaving no size-based reclaim trigger at all

materialize_tickets bypasses cache.acquire and never calls add_bytes, so tickets-<sha> entries (~620 MiB each, the largest entries in the store) are invisible to byte-accounting despite being marked evictable
the snapshot store lacks a configurable size-cap knob, leaving it append-only on most hosts and vulnerable to disk pressure on hosts that do run the janitor
two independent root causes prevent size-driven garbage collection: the backstop trigger does not exist in _gc_pass, and the dominant entry kind is not byte-accounted
cache.byte_total is under-counted by the amount materialize_tickets contributes, so even if a cap trigger were implemented it would fire against an inaccurate total
ADR 0005 D2 and cache.acquire's docstring establish an obligation to account bytes exactly once incrementally; RC-2 is a defect that violates this stated invariant
